notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS exploring Redwood Hosted API for rapid MVP then migrate to Dedicated for steady state. Team cares about predictable cost, EU data residency for a subset of customers, and strong latency SLOs for agent workflows.

Background & decision drivers:
- CTO (A. Reynolds) ran initial hosted integration (chat + embeddings) during Q4; quick implementation via SDK, 2 devs, ~3 days.
- POC showed host_api latency p95 ~120-140ms for text gen at 512 tokens (demo env). Embedding batch 100 reqs average 85ms.
- Primary ask: Dedicated commit to reduce per-token unit cost, guarantee capacity for peak metrics (Black Friday-like spikes for retail customers).
- Cost sensitivity: CPO wants predictable monthly committed spend with predictable overage caps. Prefer commit + burst model rather than pure on-demand.

POC & perf notes:
- POC lasted 4 weeks: integrated chat assistant (support-agent) and semantic search (doc-search).
- Measured sustained throughput: 90 qps for embeddings with batching; spikes to 240 qps for short periods.
- Latency SLO targets: p95 < 200ms for chat generation (95% of requests), target cold-start < 500ms.
- Observability: wants token-level cost breakdown in Console; tracing hooks to tie requests to internal request_id.

Pricing / packaging negotiation points (live):
- Preferred commit: starting 24-month reserved capacity with a 60-80% commit of forecasted baseline. Redwood offered two tiers: 60% commit at 25% discount, 80% at 37% discount + extended burst buffer.
- Burst agreement: customer needs bursts to 2x baseline for 48 hours/month for product launches. Request: guaranteed burst capacity on Dedicated (soft guarantees) and documented fallback to hosted API for overflow.
- Overage: current proposal: overage billed at 1.6x committed unit rate. Customer asks for a stepped overage (1.2x first 20% over, 1.5x >20%) and monthly cap equal to 15% of committed spend.
- Ramp schedule: 3-phase migration plan over 6 months: pilot (1 month, 20% traffic), ramp (months 2-4, 50-80%), full cutover month 6. Wants automatic autoscale policy tweaks during ramp.
- SLA & credits: require 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated endpoints used in production agent flows. Also need response SLAs for SE/infra escalation during major incidents.

Security / compliance:
- Infosec already completed initial questionnaire; outstanding items: KMS key import process, evidence of SOC2 control implementation, EU data residency enforcement for EU customer segment.
- Legal flagged data processing addendum for sub-processor list and liability caps.

Commercial status & asks from AE/SE: 
- AE/Maya: push for a 3% increase to discount if customer signs 36-month commitment instead of 24. Also ask Finance to consider blended rate for first 3 months during ramp.
- SE/Diego: needs confirmation on kernel/quantization options supported on Dedicated (for cost-targeting) and whether model pinning across variants preserved in failover.
- Customer: wants example contract language for burst/overage protections and a sample ramp pricing schedule to present to procurement.
